content:
marco: quick follow-up on the kernel-selection RFC — we merged most of the patch but I want to lock down the flip process for per-model kernel enables. how do people feel about a two-stage flip (canary -> gradual percent -> global) plus an enforced fallback list per model?

carrie: +1 on two-stage. can we add an automated rollback trigger based on p95 latency and a small eval prompt set?

ivan: yes. propose thresholds: p95 latency increase > 15% OR error-rate > 0.5% over a 5m window should auto-rollback. keep manual override for infra emergencies.

marco: sounds good. ivan, can you file a small monitoring task? need exact metrics and alert channels.

ivan: filed: infra#2345. alert to #eng-oncall + paging policy. I'll add a histogram for token latency and a gauge for kernel-fallbacks-per-minute.

tamika: one caveat: some models are latency-sensitive but can tolerate small quality diffs, others are quality-first. we should support per-model policies: {mode: "latency" | "quality", acceptable_delta: 0.XX}.

carrie: agreed. that maps to kernel preference lists and fallback ordering. also want a safe-mode that forces 'compat_attn' for whole customer if any privacy flag set.

marco: good call. quick config sketch for per-model flag (yaml):

```yaml
feature_flags:
  per_model_kernel:
    enabled: true
    default_kernel: "fast_attn_v2"
    policy: "latency"  # latency | quality
    acceptable_delta: 0.10
    fallback_order: ["fast_attn_v2", "compat_attn", "cpu_attn"]
    canary_percent: 5
    gradual_steps: [10, 25, 50, 100]
```

marco: that give a concrete starting point. question: how do we express compatibility constraints? e.g., some quantized kernels can't run > seq_len 4096.

ivan: add constraints field:

```yaml
    constraints:
      max_seq_len: 4096
      supported_qtypes: ["int8", "fp16"]
```

tamika: also include a telemetry whitelist to ensure we collect representative prompts during canary. otherwise canary sees only short demos and misses tail cases.

carrie: operational note: deploy-bot should announce kernel flips with a link to rollout dashboard and a short diff of kernel params. ops-bot should annotate customer impacts.

deploy-bot: build #kernel-switch-2025 queued, changelist: feat(kernel): per-model flip API + telemetry hooks. CI: green. :rocket:

ops-bot: scheduled canary for 2025-02-11T13:00Z to 5% for models tagged "staging". oncall: @eng-oncall. docs: /runbooks/kernel-flip.md

marco: final topic: fallback behavior when kernel reports recoverable error (OOM, kernel-crash). do we retry same kernel after backoff, or immediately switch to next fallback?

ivan: prefer immediate switch to next fallback for user request, and async ticket to repro + attempt retry on background. avoids user-visible latency spikes.

tamika: +1. must add a metric for fallback-churn per model and a circuit breaker: if > N fallbacks in 5m then quarantined and pinned to stable kernel until manual review.

carrie: action items:
- ivan: implement alerts + metrics (infra#2345)
- tamika: update policy schema with mode/constraints/telemetry whitelist (data#121)
- marco: add deploy-bot announcement + runbook link into the merge checklist
- safety: confirm any privacy impact for per-customer safe-mode (cc @safety)

safety: will review safe-mode rules today and confirm if any additional audit logs required.

marco: thanks everyone — i'll update the RFC follow-up checklist and convert config sketches into a small protobuf schema. ping me if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
